## Easing default corrected

The default Blend width is now **0.1 instead of 0.2**, matching the documented default in both C# and GDScript. At the neutral split (`Skew`/`skew = 0.5`), mixed In/Out easing curves now join over **45%–55%** of progress rather than 40%–60%.

- The correction applies to tween options, configuration builders, and standalone easing evaluation. The easing playground and shared conformance fixtures use the same default.
- Mixed easing pairs that rely on the default may look different near their join. Set `Blend = 0.2` in C# or `blend = 0.2` in GDScript to preserve the previous shape.
- Matching In/Out families at the neutral split retain their conventional shape.

## Documentation and examples

- Reorganize the C# and GDScript API references around a tween's lifecycle, with dedicated pages for callbacks and starting playback. Previous modes and enums page URLs redirect to their replacements.
- Add a visual easing-family reference covering curve families and numbered variants.
- Improve interactive demonstrations of timelines, playback, ownership, fill modes, timing, and endpoint variations, alongside clearer code comparisons and syntax-sugar examples.
- Add class headings and section links to the GDScript property catalog's table of contents.

## Downloads

- **Godot addon:** `tweens.gd-0.1.3-beta.zip` includes C# and GDScript sources and prebuilt native libraries. Requires Godot 4.7.2; C# additionally requires Godot .NET and .NET 8 or later.
- **Compiled C# package:** `tweens.gd.0.1.3-beta.nupkg`, targeting .NET 8 and .NET 10, with symbols in `tweens.gd.0.1.3-beta.snupkg`.

**Full changelog:** [v0.1.2-beta…v0.1.3-beta](https://github.com/outfox/tweens.gd/compare/v0.1.2-beta...v0.1.3-beta)
